column2: Who in two ways is the best Vritra-slayer, known, Indra, the hundred-powered; come to the pressed soma with your bay horses.
For you, Vritra-slayer, are the drinker of these somas; come to the pressed soma with your bay horses.
The sages brought forth a fair praise, a prayer, for the wide-going great Indra; the steadfast do not break his vows.
The songs have set Indra, whose wrath is unyielded, as king in order to overcome; they swelled with great strength for the bay-horsed.
May I be able to teach this one, honoring day by day, to wealth somewhere; for there is nothing other than you, bounteous one, no better kinsman, and no father.
Hear the call of the drinker of the stone-pressed soma; heed the thought of the sage who sings; make our service nearest; may we be joined.
I do not forget your songs of the swift, nor the good praise of the mighty one, knowing; I always speak your name of self-glory.
Many are your pressings among men; the wise one invokes you alone; do not send us far away, bounteous one, for long.

Honor well this Indra with strength in front of his chariot; the world-maker even in the near, in the meeting, in battles, Vritra-slayer; be our urger; let the bowstrings of our enemies break on their bows.
You released the rivers downward and slew the serpent; unfoed, Indra, you were born; you nourish all desirable things; we embrace you; let the bowstrings of our enemies break on their bows.

Let all grudges and enemies vanish from our thoughts; you throw the weapon at the foe who wishes to slay us, Indra; whatever bounty you have given — let the bowstrings of our enemies break on their bows.
Let the praiser be wealthy, one like you, bounteous and wealthy; flow forth, O bay-horsed, to the pressed soma.
Do not give us up, Indra, to the one who would drink us up, nor to the violent; teach with your powers, O powerful one.
Here the wheel-rim of these is shaken like the wolf shakes the sheep; go to heaven, to that heaven which rules, O Vasu of the day.
Let the soma-pressing stone sound for you here and bring you with its voice; go to heaven, to that heaven which rules, O Vasu of the day.
Flow, Soma, delighting Indra, most honeyed.
Those pressed, wise, bright ones released themselves to Vayu.
They have been released for the gods' feast, like chariots seeking strength.

I regard Agni as the priest, the giver, the son of the Vasu, born of strength, Jatavedas, the sage; the god who goes well-sacrificing with his high-reaching grace to the gods, after the shining of the ghee, of the bright-flamed one, the poured butter.

We sacrificers call you, best of sacrificers, eldest of the Angirases, O sage, with thoughts, with the sages, bright one, with thoughts; like the sky surrounding, the priest of the peoples; of shining hair, the bull, whom these clans help for speed.

For he shines with great strength with golden brightness, overcoming harmers, like an axe overcoming harmers; whose firm one, even in the clash, is heard like a forest; he subdues and restrains the foe, he does not go, he does not go from the bow.
Agni, your fame and vigor are great; your flames shine, O wealth-shiner; great-radiant, with strength you give praiseworthy force to the giver, O seer.
Of purifying splendor, bright splendor, undiminished splendor, you rise with light; a son moving between his parents, you protect and fill both worlds.
O grandson of strength, Jatavedas, rejoice with good praises, set by thought; in you the nourishments, of many forms, of wondrous help, unborn, have been gathered.
Moving, spread yourself, Agni, with creatures; for us wealth, immortal; you shine with the beautiful body; you fill the beautiful skill.
The maker of the sacrifice, the wise, dwelling in great bounty; you bestow the fortunate gift of the desirable, great strength, the victorious wealth.
The people in front set the truthful, great, all-seeing Agni for favor; listening, most widespread, divine; with song, in human ages.
That man crosses over, O Agni, with your helps and heroic deeds of strength — he whose friendship you have favored.
Your blue-gray drop is placed seasonally, kindled, sharply; you are dear to the great dawns; you shine in the dwellings of the night.
The plants held him as the seasonal embryo; the waters, the mothers, begot Agni; the trees and the herbs, and those pregnant ones, give birth to him daily.
Agni flows for Indra; he shines bright in heaven; he is born like a great one.
Him who is awake the verses desire; him who is awake the chants approach; him who is awake this Soma says, "I dwell in your friendship."
Agni is awake; the verses desire him; Agni is awake; the chants approach him; Agni is awake; this Soma says to him, "I dwell in your friendship."
Homage to the friends who sat before; homage to those who sit together; I yoke the hundred-footed speech.
I yoke the hundred-footed speech, sing in the thousand-fold course: Gayatra, Traishtubha, Jagata.
The Gayatra, Traishtubha, Jagata — all forms gathered; the gods have made their dwellings.
Agni is light, light is Agni; Indra is light, light is Indra; the Sun is light, light is the Sun.
Return again with strength, again, Agni, with food and life; again protect us from distress.
Return with wealth, Agni, swell with the stream, all-formed, on all sides.
If I were as you are, Indra, alone ruling over wealth, my praiser would be a friend with cattle.
May I be able to teach this wise man, and wish to give to him, O lord of powers, when I would be lord of cattle.
Your cow, Indra, truth, gives to the sacrificer who presses, swelling, milking cattle and horses.
You waters are indeed bringers of comfort; place us in strength, for great delight and sight.
Give us here a share of your most auspicious essence, like longing mothers.
We come fully to that for whose dwelling you quicken us, O waters; and you beget us.
And, Wind, you are our father, and our brother and our friend; make us live.
O Wind, the immortality that lies hidden in your house — give us of that for life.
The racer, all-formed, carrying a golden womb, the fair-winged, taking the seasonal radiance of the sun, clothed by himself, the swift, begot wisdom.
Seed lay in the waters, of all forms, the splendor that came into being on the earth; measuring his own greatness in the air, the seed of the bull-horse roars.
Clothed in a thousand yoked things, the sacrifice has held the radiance of the sun; giver of thousands, of hundreds, bountiful, upholder of heaven, lord of the world.
The Gandharva has stood high in the heaven, carrying wondrous weapons toward us; wearing a fragrant garment to be seen, he, like heaven, begot dear things.
When the drop goes to the sea, seeing with the vulture's eye in the rite; the radiant, desiring with bright flame, made dear things in the third sphere.
Swift, sharpening, like a terrible bull, the repeated smiter, the shaker of peoples; roaring, unwinking, the one hero, Indra has conquered a hundred armies together.
With roaring, unwinking, victorious, with the battle-cry, unshakable, bold — conquer with Indra, withstand it, O men, in battle with the bull with arrows in hand.
He with arrow-handed ones, with quiver-bearing ones, the master, joined, Indra fights with his troop; the soma-drinker, with strong arms, fierce-bowed, the shooter of the arrows set on the string.
Brihaspati, go round with your chariot, slaying demons, driving away enemies; breaking armies, crushing in battle, conquering, protector of our chariots.
Strong-known, mighty, brave, victorious, a racer, overcoming, fierce; heroic and bold, born of strength, Indra, mount the victorious cattle-finding chariot.
Shake the cow-pen, the finder of cattle, thunderbolt-armed, victorious in battle, crushing with might; follow him, kinsmen, as heroes, and take hold with him, friends — Indra.
Plunging into the cattle-pens with strength, pitiless hero, hundred-furious Indra, hard to move, conquering armies, unconquerable; may he protect our army in the battles.
May Indra be the leader of them, Brihaspati, sacrifice, soma, go before; of the divine armies breaking and conquering, may the Maruts go first.
The strong wrath of Indra the bull, of king Varuna, of the Adityas and Maruts, great-minded, the shakers of the worlds, the cry of the conquering gods has risen.
Bounteous one, raise up our weapons and the spirits of our brave ones; Vritra-slayer, raise up the strengths of the strong, the cries of our conquering chariots.
May Indra be with our banners in the meetings; may our arrows conquer; may our heroes be superior; may the gods protect us in the calls.
That army of the enemies, O Maruts, which advances against us contending with might — hide it with darkness, no way, so that none of them knows another.
Bewildering their minds, seize their limbs and go; go forth, burn; with griefs in their hearts may the enemies be joined to blinding darkness.
Go forth, conquer, men; may Indra give you shelter; let your arms be fierce, unassailable as you are.
Cast loose, fly away, O arrow sharpened by prayer; go to the enemies, fall upon them; leave none of them.
Let the vultures and fair-winged birds follow them; let that army be food for vultures; let none of them be freed, nor the thief; Indra, let birds follow all of them.
O bounteous Indra, toward the enemy army that attacks us — Vritra-slayer Indra, and Agni, burn it both in turn.
Where the arrows fall like youths with tufts of hair, there may Brahmanaspati and Aditi give us shelter, give us shelter always.
Drive away the demons, drive away the enemies, break the jaws of Vritra; drive away the anger, Indra Vritra-slayer, of the enemy who assails.
Drive away our enemies, Indra; restrain downward those who attack; send to lower darkness him who assails us.
The two arms of Indra are strong, young, unassailable, fair-faced, irresistible; yoke them first when the yoking comes, by which the great might of the Asuras was won.
I cover your vital parts with armor; may King Soma clothe you with immortality; may Varuna make it wider than wide for you; may the gods rejoice after you, the victor.
Be blind, O enemies, headless like snakes; of you who are driven by Agni may Indra strike the best one by one.
Whoever, our own kinsman or stranger, wishes to slay us — may all the gods confound him; prayer is the armor within me, shelter is the armor within me.
Terrible like a wild beast, dwelling in the mountains, you come from far, from the farthest; sharpen the sharp thunderbolt, Indra, strike the enemies, drive away the foes.

May we hear with our ears what is auspicious, O gods; may we see with our eyes what is auspicious, O worshipful ones; with firm limbs and bodies, praising, may we attain the life appointed by the gods.
